newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil markets weaker after bearish US data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil markets weaker after bearish US data.

text.p: World oil markets were slightly weaker on Wednesday on bearish oil data from the United States and the prospect of a speedy renewal of Iraq's "oil-for-food" deal.
Brent Blend crude, the world benchmark grade, was down 14 cents a barrel at $18.76 at 1354 GMT in London and just under the $19 average of the past three months.

Oil stocks rose nearly 17 million barrels in the United States last week to stand some 24 million barrels above year-ago levels, according to figures released on Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
The API also reported that U.S. refineries were running nearly flat out and produced a record 8.195 million barrels of gasoline last week.
Gasoline demand in the U.S. is forecast to grow by 2.5 percent this summer and is one of the few bullish factors underpinning the wider oil market.
"I still think gasoline will provide some support. The market has been very much U.S. product led recently," said Mehdi Varzi oil analayst at Kleinwort Benson in London.
But he warned "any further gasoline builds should push the price lower" and saw "no shortage of crude oil worldwide".
The United Nations Security Council may also vote to extend Iraq's "oil-for-food" deal as early as Wednesday.

A vote to allow Iraq to sell another $2 billion worth of oil over the next six months had been tentatively scheduled for Friday but U.S. officals are expecting to wave it through, possibly later on Wednesday.
The deal, an exception to the economic sanctions in place since Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990, expires on June 7.
Under its terms Baghdad was allowed to use oil earnings to buy food, medicines and other necessities for ordinary Iraqis who have suffered under sanctions.
But while the prospect of fresh Iraqi exports was providing a bearish backdrop to the market, oil dealers have long been expecting the deal to be rolled over.
